bc_the_playground.blurb: A small, family-minded sport crag in the forest east of Squamish, tucked beside a logging spur only a minute's stroll from the road. It holds 14 short routes, mostly sport with a few top-rope lines, running from gentle slab on the left to steeper, near-vertical climbing on the right. Grades start in the 5.4 range and top out around 5.11, with the bulk of the routes landing between 5.6 and 5.10. A bolted easy line on the far left gives a safe way to the anchors for setting up top ropes. Trees at the base shade the wall in summer, and the quick access makes it a handy pick for beginners, kids and short outings.

bc_the_hermitage.blurb: A compact sport wall in the Cheakamus Canyon climbing zone north of Squamish, set among old firs and a short way from the popular Echo Beach wall. All 14 routes are bolted and fall between 5.10 and 5.13, with the largest group at 5.12, so this is a place for strong sport climbers rather than newcomers. The lines are shorter than on its neighbour, but the stone is smooth and water-worn, rewarding short, powerful and dynamic moves instead of long endurance pitches. The walk in takes about 20 minutes and includes some exposed ledge traversing, so expect an adventurous start to the day.

bc_flake_cliff.blurb: A pale, gently overhanging cliff in the Gillies Creek corner of the Skaha Bluffs, on the south side of the climbing zone above Skaha Lake. It carries 14 routes, nearly all of them bolted, plus a single gear line. This is a wall for people who already climb well: nothing is easier than the low 5.10s, ten of the routes sit around 5.12, and a few go beyond into the 5.13 range. The cliff is somewhat sheltered from wind, and the surrounding canyons see fewer people than the main crags despite short walks. Plan a hike of a few hundred metres on an old road, then a faint side trail marked by a small rock pile.

bc_diamondback_south.blurb: The lower-grade side of the Diamondback cluster in the southern part of Skaha Bluffs, a short uphill walk from the upper parking area. Fourteen routes, eleven bolted and three on gear, cover a friendly spread: a handful of 5.8 and 5.9 lines, several 5.10s, a few 5.11s and one 5.12. The harder climbing lives around the corner on the east side, so this face works well as a warm-up or for climbers working through the moderate grades. Because the approach is so brief, it can be busy on good weekends, and the surrounding cliffs add plenty of nearby options if it is crowded.

bc_foreplay_south.blurb: A short, easygoing wall at the south end of Foreplay Cliff in the Skaha Bluffs, on the Penticton side of the park. Fourteen routes are listed, mostly bolted sport with a couple on gear, and the grading is friendly: a single 5.7, six at 5.9, a couple of 5.10s and a handful of 5.11s. Many lines are well protected and the top is easy to reach, which makes the wall a good spot for setting up top ropes and for climbers stepping up through the 5.8 to 5.10 range. The neighbouring main cliff stays shaded until early afternoon and holds much harder lines.

bc_enchanted.blurb: The first cluster of boulders met on the walk into Paradise Valley, north of Squamish, with a fairytale feel among the trees. It is a bouldering-only spot with 14 problems spread over a wide range, from a VB or V0 warm-up through a middle section dominated by V4s, up to a few hard tests in the V6 to V10 range. Easier problems are modest in number, so this is better suited to climbers around V4 and above than to beginners.
